questions.q: 'I ___ (finish) my homework just now' vs 'I ___ (finish) it an hour ago.'
questions.a: have finished / finished — 'just now' bridges to now; 'an hour ago' is a dead time-stamp → simple past. A wrong answer 'have finished' for the second shows the dated-perfect error.

questions.q: Fix: 'She has visited Agra last year.'
questions.a: 'She visited Agra last year' — 'last year' is a closed box; present perfect cannot carry a finished time. A wrong answer keeping 'has visited' shows the signal-word rule isn't applied.

questions.q: Which fits: 'I ___ never ___ (see) the Taj Mahal.'
questions.a: 'have never seen' — 'never' is a perfect signal (life experience up to now). 'Seen' must be V3, not 'saw' — 'have saw' is a broken participle error.

questions.q: It differs from simple past, which is ______: 'I finished yesterday' — done, closed, dated.
Fill in the blank: Present perfect ______ a past action to NOW: 'I have finished' — the work is done AND matters now.

Fill in the blank: The bridge rule: ______ perfect = past action with a bridge to now; simple past = past action in a closed box. 'I have lost my keys' — still lost (bridge). 'I lost my keys yesterday' — the story ended yesterday (box).
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student chooses present perfect vs simple past using the connection-to-now test and signal words, forms have/has + V3 correctly, and knows yesterday/ago words KILL the perfect.
